title: Remove a Third to Tilt the Halves
statement:
You get an array nums with exactly 3n elements. Remove any n of them. The 2n elements left keep their order and are cut into a first half (the first n) and a second half (the last n).

Return the smallest possible value of sum(first half) − sum(second half). The value may be negative.

examples.why: Remove the 5: then 1 − 9 = −8. Removing the 9, the biggest value, would leave 5 − 1 = 4.
Every choice leaves two halves with the same sum.

hints: After removing n elements, there is a split point: the first half comes from nums[0..i) and the second half from nums[i..3n). The split point i can be anywhere from n to 2n.
For a fixed split point, the best first half is the n smallest values on the left and the best second half is the n largest values on the right.
Compute leftMin[i] for every split with a max-heap of size n sweeping left to right, and rightMax[i] with a min-heap of size n sweeping right to left. Answer = min over i of leftMin[i] − rightMax[i].

explain.intuition:
Whatever you remove, the first half ends somewhere and the second half starts after it. Name the split point i: the first half is taken from nums[0..i) and the second from nums[i..3n). Both sides need at least n elements, so n ≤ i ≤ 2n. Once i is fixed the two sides are independent: make the first sum as small as possible (its n smallest values) and the second as large as possible (its n largest values).

Recomputing these for every split is too slow, but both change by one element per step. Sweep left to right with a max-heap holding the n smallest values seen so far: push the new value, pop the biggest if the heap grows past n, and keep the running sum. Sweep right to left with a min-heap for the n largest. Then combine the two arrays.
steps: Left sweep: push nums[0..n) into a max-heap and record left[n] as their sum. For i from n to 2n − 1, push nums[i], pop the largest, update the sum, and store left[i + 1].
Right sweep: push nums[2n..3n) into a min-heap, record right[2n]. For i from 2n − 1 down to n, push nums[i], pop the smallest, and store right[i].
Return the minimum of left[i] − right[i] for i from n to 2n.
pitfalls: Removing the n largest values. That shrinks the second half too, as the second example shows.
Using the wrong heap direction. Keeping the n smallest values needs a max-heap, so the biggest of them can be thrown out.
Missing a split point: i runs from n to 2n inclusive, which is n + 1 positions.

solutions.title: Sort both sides for every split
solutions.idea: For each split point, sort the left part to take its n smallest values and the right part to take its n largest.

solutions.title: Prefix and suffix heaps
solutions.idea: A max-heap sweep gives the smallest n-sum of every prefix; a min-heap sweep gives the largest n-sum of every suffix.

followups: Return which elements to remove, not only the best value.
The halves may have sizes a and b with a + b fixed, not n and n. What changes in the sweeps?
